sentences.text: Notosuchus was a terrestrial animal that lived approximately 85 million years ago during the Santonian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
It was relatively small in size compared to many other crocodylomorphs.
Its skull was triangular in dorsal view, featuring a high snout that was quadrangular in cross-section with anterior external nares.
The teeth of N. terrestris possessed exceptionally thick cementum compared to other crocodylomorphs.
Some authors infer the presence of feeding mechanisms in Notosuchus that contrast with those of other crocodyliform groups, including modern crocodilians.
Notosuchus was first named in 1896 and holds the distinction of being the first known notosuchian.
Fossilized remains of Notosuchus have been found in the Bajo de la Carpa Formation in Patagonia, Argentina.
A second species, N. lepidus, was named in 1957.
Analysis allowed researchers to infer a terrestrial lifestyle with an upright posture, propalinal jaw movement, and omnivorous or even herbivorous habits.
The dentition of N. terrestris was heterodont, consisting of incisiform, caniniform, and molariform teeth.
It was characterized by heterodont dentition with a wide range of morphologies in its posterior teeth.
Bonaparte considered Notosuchia to be a suborder of Protosuchia based on basicranial characteristics in his 1991 study.
Notosuchus shares three derived dental characters with Mariliasuchus amarali and Sphagesaurus huenei, suggesting these three taxa are more closely related to each other than to other crocodyliforms.
The parent group of Notosuchus is Sphagesauria.
These terrestrial animals lived approximately 85 million years ago during the Coniacian or Santonian stages of the Late Cretaceous.
The time range for Notosuchus is the Santonian, spanning from 85.7 to 83.6 million years ago.
